es: Reconocer qué busca cada pregunta de una entrevista (experiencia, hipótesis, motivación, límite, ampliación) y qué tipo de respuesta exige, incluso cuando la intención va implícita.

vocabulary.es: hacer que alguien revele o desarrolle algo

teaching.en: An interviewer rarely asks a question for its own sake; behind each one lies a quality the committee wants to gauge.
teaching.es: Un entrevistador rara vez pregunta por preguntar; detrás de cada pregunta hay una cualidad que el comité quiere evaluar.
teaching.explanationEs: Antes de responder, pregúntate qué cualidad intenta medir la pregunta.
segments: An interviewer rarely asks a question for its own sake; behind
each one lies a quality the committee wants to gauge.
teaching.audioText: An interviewer rarely asks a question for its own sake; behind each one lies a quality the committee wants to gauge.

teaching.en: Tell me about a challenge you faced asks for evidence from the past, so a strong applicant answers with a real episode.
teaching.es: «Cuéntame un reto al que te enfrentaste» pide evidencia del pasado, así que un candidato sólido responde con un episodio real.
teaching.explanationEs: Tell me about a… exige una historia en pasado, no un principio general.
segments: Tell me about a challenge you faced asks for evidence from
the past, so a strong applicant answers with a real episode.
teaching.audioText: Tell me about a challenge you faced asks for evidence from the past, so a strong applicant answers with a real episode.

teaching.en: A hypothetical question may leave you feeling put on the spot, yet it tests your judgement rather than your record.
teaching.es: Una pregunta hipotética puede hacerte sentir en un aprieto, pero pone a prueba tu criterio y no tu historial.
teaching.explanationEs: What would you do if…? (if + pasado) no pide hechos: pide razonar en voz alta.
segments: A hypothetical question may leave you feeling put on the
spot, yet it tests your judgement rather than your record.
teaching.audioText: A hypothetical question may leave you feeling put on the spot, yet it tests your judgement rather than your record.

teaching.en: Questions about underlying motivation, such as what first drew you to this scholarship, invite personal reasons rather than a summary of the brochure.
teaching.es: Las preguntas sobre la motivación, como qué te atrajo de esta beca, invitan a dar razones personales y no a resumir el folleto.
teaching.explanationEs: Motivation busca el porqué íntimo; repetir datos públicos suena a respuesta vacía.
segments: Questions about underlying motivation, such as what first drew you to this
scholarship, invite personal reasons rather than a summary of the brochure.
teaching.audioText: Questions about underlying motivation, such as what first drew you to this scholarship, invite personal reasons rather than a summary of the brochure.

teaching.en: When asked about a limitation, a candid applicant names a genuine weakness and explains how she is working to overcome it.
teaching.es: Cuando le preguntan por una limitación, una candidata franca nombra un punto débil genuino y explica cómo trabaja para superarlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Un límite se responde con franqueza y con un plan de mejora, no con un defecto disfrazado de virtud.
segments: When asked about a limitation, a candid applicant names a genuine
weakness and explains how she is working to overcome it.
teaching.audioText: When asked about a limitation, a candid applicant names a genuine weakness and explains how she is working to overcome it.

teaching.en: Could you elaborate on that? signals that your answer was too general and that the interviewer hopes to draw out more detail.
teaching.es: «¿Podrías ampliar eso?» indica que tu respuesta fue demasiado general y que el entrevistador espera sacar más detalles.
teaching.explanationEs: Elaborate on y draw out detail: pide concreción, no es una crítica.
segments: Could you elaborate on that? signals that your answer was too
general and that the interviewer hopes to draw out more detail.
teaching.audioText: Could you elaborate on that? signals that your answer was too general and that the interviewer hopes to draw out more detail.

prompt.es: Une cada pregunta de entrevista con lo que realmente busca.

pairs: Talk me through a decision you came to regret.

pairs.es: Un episodio real y tu capacidad de autocrítica

pairs: How would you respond if your funding were cut mid-year?

pairs.es: Tu criterio ante un supuesto, no un hecho

pairs: What was it that first drew you to this scholarship?

pairs.es: Tus razones personales, no datos del folleto

pairs: Which of your skills would you say still falls short?

pairs.es: Una limitación real y qué haces con ella

feedback.es: Cada pregunta se descifra por su arranque: una decisión pasada pide autocrítica, un supuesto mide criterio, «drew you to» busca razones y «falls short» apunta a un límite.

hint.es: Mira el verbo y el tiempo de cada pregunta: pasado real, would, razón personal o carencia.

prompt.es: ¿Qué espera encontrar el entrevistador tras esta petición?

choices.text: A promise that the applicant will avoid difficulty in future.
More detail about what the applicant actually found hardest.
A sign that the project was badly managed overall.

feedback.es: «Could you elaborate?» pide que concretes lo que quedó vago; no acusa ni exige promesas.

hint.es: Fíjate en qué pide exactamente la segunda frase: que desarrolles lo que dijiste.

origin.text: You described the project as a difficult year. Could you elaborate on that? I am interested in what exactly you found hardest, and what you would do differently now.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es una pregunta hipotética porque pone a prueba tu criterio.»

feedback.es: Suppose/would… if plantean una situación imaginaria: por eso la pregunta es hypothetical y mide criterio.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo de la lista que describe una situación imaginaria.

origin.text: The interviewer said, “Suppose the funding were cut tomorrow. How would you respond?” It is a ___ question, because it tests judgement rather than experience.

prompt.es: Escucha el episodio y elige qué error comete la candidata.

choices.text: She answers a question about motivation with a plan for overcoming her own weakness.
She answers a request for more detail with a general statement about herself.
She answers a question about motivation with facts anyone could find in the brochure.

feedback.es: La pregunta busca razones personales, pero ella resume el folleto: datos públicos que cualquiera encontraría, no una motivación propia.

origin.audio: Asked what first drew her to the scholarship, the applicant spent a full minute listing what the brochure says about the course: its staff, its buildings and its reputation. The committee chair listened politely, but it was clear that she had been hoping for something personal, a reason that only this applicant could give.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo reacciona la candidata ante la pregunta del entrevistador?

choices.text: It is a hypothetical question; she answers it with a detailed story.
It is a motivation question; she avoids giving any real reason.
It is a leading question; she accepts its premise without any doubt.
It is a leading question; she concedes a point but keeps her view.

feedback.es: El entrevistador empuja hacia una sola respuesta (leading question), y ella admite algo con «I see the point» pero añade su reserva con «although».

origin.text: Interviewer: Surely you would agree that anyone serious about this scholarship would give up their weekends to study? Applicant: Well, I see the point, although I would say that rest matters too.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los buenos entrevistadores usan el silencio para sacar detalles.»

feedback.es: Draw out es el verbo frasal para sacar a la luz información que el otro no da espontáneamente.

origin.text: Skilled interviewers rarely rush. They use silence and short follow-up questions to draw ___ details that an applicant would not offer freely.

prompt.es: Empareja cinco preguntas de entrevista con la intención que esconden.

pairs: Is there a part of the role you feel unsure about?

pairs.es: Busca una limitación y tu franqueza

pairs: Suppose two referees gave you opposite advice. What then?

pairs.es: Plantea un supuesto para medir tu criterio

pairs: Describe a time you disagreed with your boss.

pairs.es: Pide un episodio real del pasado

pairs: What would keep you going when the work grows boring?

pairs.es: Indaga tu motivación profunda

pairs: You mentioned a difficult year. Could you say more?

pairs.es: Te pide ampliar una respuesta demasiado general

feedback.es: Cada pregunta delata su intención: «unsure about» apunta a un límite, «suppose» abre un supuesto, «a time» pide un caso real, «keep you going» busca motivación y «say more» pide ampliar.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la entrevistadora plantea a veces preguntas tendenciosas.

choices.text: To see whether the candidate accepts a premise or politely challenges it.
To make the candidate feel relaxed before the harder questions begin.
To test whether the candidate has read the course description closely.
To hurry the candidate towards the answer she already expects to hear.

feedback.es: La exentrevistadora dice que lo hace «to see whether a candidate will quietly agree or politely push back»: quiere ver si el candidato acepta la premisa o la discute.

origin.audio: On this week's episode, a former scholarship officer explained what she really listens for. Candidates, she said, prepare for the questions they fear, such as the one about weaknesses, and then stumble over the ones that look simple. Where do you see yourself in five years? sounds like small talk, but it is her way of gauging whether an applicant's ambitions fit the course. She also admitted that she sometimes asks a leading question on purpose, simply to see whether a candidate will quietly agree or politely push back. Silence, she added, costs her nothing, and it often draws out the most honest answers.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere la autora del correo sobre los candidatos de la beca?

choices.text: That hypothetical questions should be dropped because candidates handle them too well.
That polished answers may hide how little some candidates reflect on themselves.
That the applicants have no real limitations worth mentioning to the committee.
That coaching is unfair and should be banned from future scholarship rounds.

feedback.es: La autora deduce que respuestas pulidas pueden decir más del entrenamiento que del carácter; no propone eliminar preguntas ni prohibir nada.

origin.text: Thanks for sitting in on Tuesday's interviews. I noticed that most applicants answered the hypothetical question fluently, yet very few could name a real limitation without rushing to a positive. That may say more about how they were coached than about their character, so I suggest we ask the second kind of question earlier next year.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su primera respuesta fue general, así que le pidió que la ampliara.»

feedback.es: Elaborate on it es la petición habitual de más detalle; expand on it también funciona con el mismo sentido.

origin.text: Her first answer was too general, so the interviewer asked her to ___ on it. “Could you give me one concrete example?” she said.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito se escribe esta nota de valoración?

choices.text: To praise the candidate's story and recommend using it in every answer.
To warn candidates that any story should be avoided in an interview.
To show that a good story answered the wrong kind of question.
To suggest that the committee rewrite its hypothetical questions.

feedback.es: La nota reconoce que la historia es sólida, pero avisa de que la pregunta era un supuesto y pedía un plan: el fallo es de intención, no de contenido.

origin.text: Feedback note: to the question about funding being cut, the candidate began with “Last year we cut costs”, a solid story, but the committee had asked for a plan. Next time, answer the question that was asked and save the anecdote for the question about challenges.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Una pregunta hipotética pone a prueba tu criterio, no tu historial.»

answer.text: A hypothetical question tests your judgement, not your record

feedback.es: La estructura contrasta lo que mide la pregunta (your judgement) con lo que no mide (your record).

prompt.es: Completa: «Esta pregunta está pensada para evaluar cómo razona el candidato.»

feedback.es: Gauge es el verbo de evaluar o calibrar una cualidad; test, assess o measure son alternativas válidas en el mismo contexto.

origin.text: Nobody enjoys being put on the spot, yet a hypothetical question is designed to ___ how an applicant reasons under pressure.

title.es: Preguntar mejor: indirectas y de sondeo

es: Formular preguntas indirectas y de sondeo con el orden afirmativo y el marcador adecuado (Could you tell me what…, To what extent…) y usarlas para concretar respuestas vagas con cortesía.

vocabulary.es: con la perspectiva que da el tiempo

teaching.en: Could you tell me what led you to choose this approach, given that two cheaper alternatives were available at the time?
teaching.es: ¿Podrías decirme qué te llevó a elegir este enfoque, dado que había dos alternativas más baratas en ese momento?
teaching.explanationEs: Tras Could you tell me, what funciona como sujeto y no necesita did.
segments: Could you tell me what led you to choose this approach,
given that two cheaper alternatives were available at the time?
teaching.audioText: Could you tell me what led you to choose this approach, given that two cheaper alternatives were available at the time?

teaching.en: I am curious whether you were able to measure the outcome, and why you chose this approach in the first place.
teaching.es: Tengo curiosidad por saber si pudiste medir el resultado y por qué elegiste este enfoque en un primer momento.
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta indirecta: whether/why + sujeto + verbo afirmativo, sin did ni inversión.
segments: I am curious whether you were able to measure the outcome,
and why you chose this approach in the first place.
teaching.audioText: I am curious whether you were able to measure the outcome, and why you chose this approach in the first place.

teaching.en: To what extent did the outcome match your plan, and what would you change with hindsight?
teaching.es: ¿Hasta qué punto coincidió el resultado con tu plan y qué cambiarías con la perspectiva que da el tiempo?
teaching.explanationEs: To what extent abre una pregunta directa: sí lleva inversión (did the outcome match).
segments: To what extent did the outcome match your
plan, and what would you change with hindsight?
teaching.audioText: To what extent did the outcome match your plan, and what would you change with hindsight?

teaching.en: A probing question, such as what precisely do you mean by successful, invites you to pin down a vague phrase.
teaching.es: Una pregunta de sondeo, como qué quieres decir exactamente con exitoso, te invita a concretar una expresión vaga.
teaching.explanationEs: Las preguntas de sondeo directas llevan auxiliar; sirven para exigir precisión.
segments: A probing question, such as what precisely do you mean
by successful, invites you to pin down a vague phrase.
teaching.audioText: A probing question, such as what precisely do you mean by successful, invites you to pin down a vague phrase.

teaching.en: Good interviewers follow up on a general answer and press for the figures that give real insight into what happened.
teaching.es: Los buenos entrevistadores profundizan en una respuesta general e insisten en las cifras que dan una idea real de lo ocurrido.
teaching.explanationEs: Follow up on + respuesta: retomas lo dicho; press for + cifras: exiges datos concretos.
segments: Good interviewers follow up on a general answer and press
for the figures that give real insight into what happened.
teaching.audioText: Good interviewers follow up on a general answer and press for the figures that give real insight into what happened.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tengo curiosidad por saber si el equipo probó la idea antes del lanzamiento.»

feedback.es: El sí/no indirecto se forma con whether (o if) + sujeto + verbo afirmativo: whether the team tested.

hint.es: Es el marcador indirecto de las preguntas de sí/no; después va el sujeto.

origin.text: Mia has read the report, but it never says how the decision was made. She asks, “I am curious ___ the team ever tested the idea before the launch.”

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Podrías explicarme por qué el equipo abandonó el primer plan?»

answer.text: Could you explain why the team abandoned the first plan

feedback.es: Tras Could you explain why el orden es afirmativo: the team abandoned, sin did.

hint.es: Empieza con la apertura cortés; después why, el sujeto y el verbo en pasado.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pregunta de sondeo consigue concretar la respuesta del ingeniero?

choices.text: To what extent the results matched the targets you had set?
To what extent did match the results the targets you had set?
To what extent did the results match the targets you had set?

feedback.es: To what extent abre una pregunta directa: lleva did + sujeto + verbo base, y obliga a cuantificar un «quite well».

hint.es: Busca la pregunta con auxiliar tras to what extent, en el orden de una pregunta directa.

origin.text: After the trial, the engineer said only, “Broadly speaking, things went quite well.” The interviewer wanted a number, not an impression.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Hasta qué punto coincidió el resultado con el plan original?»

feedback.es: To what extent pregunta por el grado o la medida; es una pregunta directa y por eso lleva did.

origin.text: The report calls the new approach a largely successful one. To what ___ did the outcome match the original plan, and who decided that it was a success?

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento y elige qué pide la moderadora al ponente.

choices.text: An assessment of which choices he would revise, now that he knows more.
An explanation of why the design was tested so late in the project.
An apology for not having involved real users in the first place.

feedback.es: «With hindsight» pide una valoración retrospectiva de sus decisiones; que admita que debió probar antes es su respuesta, no lo que ella exige.

origin.audio: After the presentation, the moderator turned to the speaker with a polite but pointed request: could you tell me what you would do differently with hindsight? The speaker paused, thanked her for the question and admitted that he would have tested the design on real users months earlier.

prompt.es: ¿Qué pregunta indirecta está bien formada?

choices.text: Could you tell me how did the department decide on the final budget?
Could you tell me how the department decided on the final budget?
Could you tell me how decided the department on the final budget?

feedback.es: Tras Could you tell me el orden es el de una frase afirmativa: how the department decided, sin did ni inversión.

origin.text: A journalist is preparing written questions for a minister and wants each one to sound polite yet precise.

prompt.es: Completa: «por qué rechazó el equipo» y «si alguien comprobó».

feedback.es: Why introduce la razón y whether el sí/no; en ambos casos el sujeto va antes del verbo, sin did.

sentences: Could you tell me ___ the team rejected the cheaper option?
I would like to know ___ anyone checked the figures before publication.

prompt.es: Escucha el programa y elige qué impresión da la presentadora.

choices.text: Polite in her wording, but happy with a general reply.
Polite in her wording, yet firm about getting a precise answer.
Sharp in her wording, and keen to catch the minister out.
Careful in her wording, though nervous about challenging a senior figure.

feedback.es: Formula peticiones corteses, pero cada vez insiste con una pregunta más precisa y no se conforma con lo general: cortés en la forma, firme en lo que exige.

origin.audio: When the minister described the scheme as a qualified success, the presenter did not move on. Instead, she pressed for detail. To what extent, she asked, did the outcome match the promises made a year earlier? The minister answered that it was too early to say, so she followed up on that: what precisely would count as success? Every indirect request, such as could you tell me what evidence you rely on, was followed by a sharper question. By the end, the minister had been tied to a clear answer without once being interrupted.

prompt.es: ¿Qué propone la editora en este correo y por qué?

choices.text: Rephrasing an accusing question, since the minister has complained about its tone.
Dropping an accusing question, since the information it asks for is not needed.
Rephrasing an accusing question, since the same information can be had more gently.
Keeping the accusing question, but asking it only after the minister has relaxed.

feedback.es: La editora reformula la pregunta como una indirecta cortés: pide lo mismo, pero deja margen para que el ministro explique y no se ponga a la defensiva.

origin.text: Thanks for the draft. Your questions are well researched, but several read like accusations. To what extent did you mislead the public? invites a defensive answer, and the interview may stall. Try Could you tell me how the campaign figures were worked out? It asks for the same information and leaves the minister room to explain.

prompt.es: Escribe una pregunta indirecta cortés para conocer el motivo del equipo.

answer.text: Could you tell me what led the team to drop the first idea?
accepted: Could you tell me what led the team to drop the first idea?
Could you explain what led the team to abandon the first idea?
Could you tell me why the team abandoned the first idea?
Could you explain why the team dropped the first idea?
Could you tell me what made the team give up the first idea?
Could you tell me why the team decided to drop the first idea?
Could you tell me what made the team abandon the first plan?

feedback.es: Una buena pregunta indirecta abre con Could you tell me/explain y sigue con what o why + sujeto + verbo afirmativo.

origin.text: Quieres saber de forma cortés qué llevó al equipo a abandonar la primera idea.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere la nota del entrevistador sobre la candidata?

choices.text: She answers sharper questions well but freezes whenever the questions are polite ones.
She knows the subject well but dislikes every kind of interview she has given.
She answered the polite questions vaguely and then the sharp ones clearly.
She is comfortable with polite questions but avoids being tied to specifics.

feedback.es: Responde con soltura a las preguntas indirectas, pero ante «To what extent» repite y cambia de tema: elude concretar, no es que desconozca el tema.

origin.text: Interview note: the candidate handled every Could you tell me… question with confidence, giving clear answers and relevant examples. When pressed with To what extent…, however, she repeated the same phrase twice and then moved on to a different subject without ever giving a figure.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Hasta qué punto cambiarías tu enfoque con la perspectiva actual?»

answer.text: To what extent would you change your approach with hindsight

feedback.es: To what extent abre una pregunta directa con would + sujeto + verbo base, y with hindsight cierra la pregunta.

prompt.es: Completa: «Quisiera concretar qué quieres decir con un buen resultado.»

feedback.es: Pin down significa concretar o precisar; nail down es la variante equivalente.

origin.text: I would like to ___ down exactly what you mean by a good outcome, because the phrase seems rather vague to me.

es: Distinguir respuestas de entrevista concretas de las vagas, detectar si a una respuesta le falta un ejemplo o un resultado medible y juzgar qué sugiere cada una sobre quien la da.

vocabulary.es: no alcanzar, quedarse corto respecto a
pasar por alto, tratar por encima

teaching.en: A vague answer leans on filler such as somehow or it went really well, which sounds confident but tells the interviewer nothing.
teaching.es: Una respuesta vaga se apoya en relleno como «de algún modo» o «salió muy bien», que suena seguro pero no le dice nada al entrevistador.
teaching.explanationEs: Somehow y went really well no dicen qué pasó ni con qué resultado.
segments: A vague answer leans on filler such as somehow or it
went really well, which sounds confident but tells the interviewer nothing.
teaching.audioText: A vague answer leans on filler such as somehow or it went really well, which sounds confident but tells the interviewer nothing.

teaching.en: To be specific, cite figures and name the action: I cut waiting times from ten days to three by creating a checklist.
teaching.es: Para ser concreto, cita cifras y nombra la acción: reduje los tiempos de espera de diez días a tres creando una lista de verificación.
teaching.explanationEs: Acción clara (a checklist) y dos cifras con from… to….
segments: To be specific, cite figures and name the action: I cut
waiting times from ten days to three by creating a checklist.
teaching.audioText: To be specific, cite figures and name the action: I cut waiting times from ten days to three by creating a checklist.

teaching.en: Aim for a measurable impact, so close with a change that can be counted: complaints fell by forty per cent in two months.
teaching.es: Busca un impacto medible, así que cierra con un cambio que se pueda contar: las quejas bajaron un cuarenta por ciento en dos meses.
teaching.explanationEs: Con verbos de cambio, la cantidad va con by (fell by), no con in.
segments: Aim for a measurable impact, so close with a change that can
be counted: complaints fell by forty per cent in two months.
teaching.audioText: Aim for a measurable impact, so close with a change that can be counted: complaints fell by forty per cent in two months.

teaching.en: You must support every claim with hard evidence, otherwise even an impressive statement will fall short of a concrete answer.
teaching.es: Debes respaldar cada afirmación con pruebas sólidas; de lo contrario, incluso una declaración impresionante no llegará a ser una respuesta concreta.
teaching.explanationEs: Hard evidence = pruebas verificables; fall short of = no llegar al nivel esperado.
segments: You must support every claim with hard evidence, otherwise even
an impressive statement will fall short of a concrete answer.
teaching.audioText: You must support every claim with hard evidence, otherwise even an impressive statement will fall short of a concrete answer.

teaching.en: A sweeping generalisation such as I always deliver on time invites the obvious follow-up: could you be more specific?
teaching.es: Una generalización excesiva como «siempre entrego a tiempo» invita a la réplica obvia: ¿podrías ser más concreto?
teaching.explanationEs: Las palabras always y never sin ejemplo suenan a relleno; el entrevistador las cuestiona.
segments: A sweeping generalisation such as I always deliver on time
invites the obvious follow-up: could you be more specific?
teaching.audioText: A sweeping generalisation such as I always deliver on time invites the obvious follow-up: could you be more specific?

teaching.en: Candidates often gloss over the weakest part of a story, yet a concrete detail there is what makes the whole answer credible.
teaching.es: Los candidatos suelen pasar por alto la parte más débil de una historia, pero un detalle concreto ahí es lo que hace creíble toda la respuesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Gloss over = tratar algo por encima; el detalle exacto en el punto flojo da credibilidad.
segments: Candidates often gloss over the weakest part of a story, yet
a concrete detail there is what makes the whole answer credible.
teaching.audioText: Candidates often gloss over the weakest part of a story, yet a concrete detail there is what makes the whole answer credible.

prompt.es: Une cada respuesta con la valoración que merece.

pairs: We did lots of things, and it all went rather well.

pairs.es: Vaga: ni acción concreta ni cifras

pairs: I changed our supplier contract, and costs fell from nine hundred to six hundred a month.

pairs.es: Concreta: acción y cifras claras

pairs: Complaints fell by half last year.

pairs.es: Resultado medible, pero sin acción concreta

pairs: I wrote a guide for new volunteers in March.

pairs.es: Ejemplo concreto, pero sin resultado medible

feedback.es: Una respuesta vaga no informa; la concreta da acción y cifras; «fell by half» es un resultado sin acción, y «I wrote a guide» es una acción sin resultado que contar.

hint.es: Pregúntate dos cosas: ¿dice qué hizo la persona? ¿da un resultado que se pueda contar?

pairs: We did lots of things, and it all went rather well.

pairs.es: Vaga: ni acción concreta ni cifras

pairs: I changed our supplier contract, and costs fell from nine hundred to six hundred a month.

pairs.es: Concreta: acción y cifras claras

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta resultaría más convincente para un entrevistador exigente?

choices.text: I streamlined the returns desk, and lost books fell from sixty to twenty in a term.
I rearranged the returns desk, and everybody agreed that the library looked so much tidier afterwards.
I helped out at the returns desk, and somehow the library ran a great deal more smoothly.

feedback.es: La convincente nombra la acción y da un cambio contable (from sixty to twenty); las otras confían en impresiones y en «somehow».

hint.es: Busca la que combina una acción con cifras y no se apoya en opiniones ni en somehow.

prompt.es: Escucha la respuesta y elige qué le falta.

choices.text: It gives a concrete action but hides the result that followed.
It gives neither a concrete action nor a result that could be counted.

feedback.es: «Helped a lot», «went really well» y «people seemed happy» son relleno: ni acción concreta ni resultado medible, y ni siquiera ante la petición de concretar aporta nada.

origin.audio: Asked about her greatest achievement, the applicant said that she had helped a lot with the school fair, that everything went really well and that people seemed happy. When the interviewer asked her to be more specific, she repeated that it had been a great team effort and moved on to her next point.

prompt.es: ¿Qué parte del texto funciona como resultado medible?

choices.text: A corner was set up for quiet reading.
The atmosphere in the library became livelier.
Weekly visits tripled within two months.

feedback.es: «From twenty to sixty» equivale a triplicar las visitas en dos meses: es el dato que se puede contar; lo demás es acción o impresión.

origin.text: I set up a reading corner in the library. Within two months, visits rose from twenty to sixty a week, and the whole space felt livelier than ever.

origin.audio: In her workshop, the careers coach played back four answers to the question: what difference did you make in your last job? The first candidate said that things generally went well and that she had helped with a lot of projects. The second described writing a guide for new staff, although he never mentioned what changed afterwards. The third said she had introduced a booking system, and that missed appointments had fallen from thirty a month to eight. The last one claimed that he always exceeded every target, which the coach called a sweeping generalisation, since he gave no example at all. Only one answer, she said, would make an interviewer stop writing and start listening.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo: ¿qué da a entender la entrenadora con su última frase?

choices.text: That a polished delivery is what holds an interviewer's attention.
That most interviewers have already decided before candidates speak.
That an interviewer listens closely only to the last answer of four.
That proof of a real change is what holds an interviewer's attention.

feedback.es: Que solo una respuesta haga «start listening» sugiere que el entrevistador solo presta atención cuando hay pruebas de un cambio real.

origin.audio: Two years ago, I organised a food drive at school. At first, nobody had signed up, so I visited every class and asked each one to choose a captain. As a result, we collected three hundred bags of food in a week. Since then, I have always started with people, not posters, because a poster asks for attention, while a person offers help.

origin.text: An applicant has just told the story of a failed fundraiser and wants to close with one sentence that states clearly what she learned from it.

prompt.es: Escribe tu respuesta: situación, acción, resultado y lección.

answer.text: Two years ago, I was in charge of the school charity concert, which was already in trouble when I took it over. Nobody had booked the hall, the posters had not been printed, and several students had lost interest. I decided to take the initiative. First, I drew up a simple checklist and asked each class to choose a captain who would report to me every Friday. Then I phoned the music teacher, who found us a hall within two days. As a result, we sold every ticket in a week, and the concert has become a yearly tradition since then. The school has raised twice as much money as before. The experience taught me that a clear plan gives people confidence. It was also a hard-won lesson about asking for help early, because the project only began to turn around once I stopped trying to do everything myself. Since then, I have used the same approach in every team I have joined.
accepted: Two years ago, I was in charge of the school charity concert, which was already in trouble when I took it over. Nobody had booked the hall, the posters had not been printed, and several students had lost interest. I decided to take the initiative. First, I drew up a simple checklist and asked each class to choose a captain who would report to me every Friday. Then I phoned the music teacher, who found us a hall within two days. As a result, we sold every ticket in a week, and the concert has become a yearly tradition since then. The school has raised twice as much money as before. The experience taught me that a clear plan gives people confidence. It was also a hard-won lesson about asking for help early, because the project only began to turn around once I stopped trying to do everything myself. Since then, I have used the same approach in every team I have joined.

Last year, I was in charge of the school garden. When I joined, nobody had watered the plants for a month, and most of the volunteers had already stopped coming. I decided to start again with a clear plan. I made a watering rota, I asked each class to choose a captain and I called the science teacher to ask for help. Within a week, the garden looked alive again. As a result, it has produced vegetables every summer since then, and the canteen has used them in its menu. The experience taught me that people help when they know exactly what they have to do. I also learned that asking for support early saves a lot of time. Today I use the same method whenever I start a new project.

feedback.es: Una respuesta completa sitúa la historia, recuerda un hecho anterior, cuenta tu acción, da un resultado que sigue vigente y cierra con una lección.

origin.text: En una entrevista para un programa de liderazgo te piden: «Cuéntame una ocasión en que lideraste un proyecto que iba mal». Escribe 210–270 palabras: situación y acción en pasado, un hecho anterior con pasado perfecto, un resultado vigente con presente perfecto y la lección aprendida.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué da a entender su última respuesta sobre el liderazgo.

choices.text: That a leader's first task is to reconcile the groups before assigning anything.
That a leader should personally take charge of every group's work.
That leaders earn respect mainly through the results of their campaigns.
That a leader's first task is to clarify who is responsible for what.

feedback.es: Al decir que lo primero es que todos sepan quién responde de qué, sugiere que liderar es dejar claras las responsabilidades, no reconciliar ni controlarlo todo.

origin.audio: During a scholarship interview, a candidate was asked about a time when she had led a team. She began with the situation: last summer, she was in charge of a clean-up campaign on the beach, and by the time she arrived, the volunteers had already split into two groups that refused to work together. She listened to both, drew up a shared plan and gave each group its own captain. The campaign has collected more rubbish every year since then. Asked what she had learned, she answered that a leader's first job is to make sure everyone knows who is responsible for what.

prompt.es: ¿Qué correcciones necesita este fragmento de una respuesta de entrevista?

Lost should be has lost, and doubled should be had doubled.
Only doubled should change, to has doubled; lost is correct here.
Only lost should change, to had lost; doubled is correct here.

feedback.es: El descenso de socios ocurrió antes de que ella fuera tesorera (had lost), y el efecto llega hasta hoy con since then (has doubled).

origin.text: By the time I became treasurer, the club lost most of its members. I visited every former member, listened to their complaints and changed the fees. Since then, membership doubled, and the accounts have been in profit every year.

title.es: Ser el invitado de un pódcast

es: Participar como invitado en un pódcast: abrir con cortesía, responder con historias estructuradas, discrepar con tacto, devolver una pregunta de sondeo al anfitrión y cerrar con una síntesis.

teaching.en: Thanks for having me; I am delighted to be your guest, and I expect your listeners to push back on some of it.
teaching.es: Gracias por invitarme; estoy encantado de ser tu invitado y espero que tus oyentes discrepen de parte de lo que diga.
teaching.explanationEs: Apertura cálida: Thanks for having me (for + -ing); push back = discrepar con tacto.

origin.text: The host has asked Tom a long question. Tom answers briefly and then smiles. “If I may turn that ___, what drew you to this episode?”

prompt.es: ¿Qué cierre resume mejor la idea principal para los oyentes?

choices.text: That is all, I think; I do not really have anything more to add to this.
Well, there were many things, and it depends, so perhaps listen to the episode again.
To wrap up, the key takeaway is simple: start small, and ask for help early.

feedback.es: Un cierre con síntesis anuncia el final (to wrap up) y deja una idea clave para los oyentes; las otras no aportan nada.

hint.es: Busca el cierre que anuncia el final y condensa una sola idea útil.

origin.text: Before we finish, the host asks, “What is the one thing you would like our listeners to remember from today?” The guest has about fifteen seconds left.

prompt.es: Escucha el fragmento y elige qué hace el invitado ante el comentario de la presentadora.

choices.text: He accepts part of the point but offers a different reading.
He agrees completely with her and drops all the plans he had made.
He rejects the question as unfair and declines to answer it at all.

feedback.es: Reconoce que es «a fair point», pero discrepa con tacto: el fracaso no cambió sus planes, le mostró cuáles merecían la pena.

origin.audio: Halfway through the recording, the host asked the guest whether failure had changed his plans. He laughed, conceded that it was a fair point, and then pushed back gently: the failure, he said, had not changed his plans so much as shown him which ones were worth keeping.

prompt.es: ¿Qué le falta a la respuesta de este invitado?

choices.text: A polite opening and a warm greeting for the listeners.
A concrete example and a result that can be counted.

feedback.es: Responde con frases de relleno («many things», «somehow», «great experience»): no hay ejemplo concreto ni resultado medible.

origin.text: Host: What was the hardest part of the project? Guest: Honestly, I did many things, and somehow it all worked out. It was a great experience for everybody, and I learned a lot from all of it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Para concluir, la idea clave para los oyentes es empezar poco a poco.»

feedback.es: To wrap up anuncia el cierre de la intervención; to sum up y to round off cumplen la misma función.

origin.text: We are nearly out of time. To ___ up, if there is one key takeaway for the listeners, it is this: start small.

prompt.es: Escribe las respuestas del invitado: apertura, historia, reto, pregunta y cierre.

answer.text: Thanks for having me. I am delighted to be your guest today. You asked what led me to start the repair café. Briefly, it began two years ago, when I noticed that my neighbours threw away broken toasters and lamps every week. When I arrived at the first meeting, nobody had brought any tools, so I drew up a short list, asked each volunteer to bring one item and borrowed a table from the library. As a result, we have repaired more than two hundred objects since then. You also asked about my biggest challenge. Honestly, it was persuading people to open up about what they could not fix. For example, in March only six neighbours came, but after I wrote a simple invitation, attendance rose from six to thirty. If I may turn that around, to what extent do your listeners already repair things at home? To wrap up, if there is one key takeaway for the listeners, it is this: start small, and ask for help early. The experience taught me that people will share skills if someone makes the first move. Thank you again for the invitation.

Thank you for inviting me. It is a pleasure to be a guest on the show. You asked why I joined the school garden. Briefly, last spring I was in charge of the vegetable beds, and nobody had watered the plants for a month. I made a watering rota, and as a result, the garden has given vegetables every summer since then. Your second question was about my biggest challenge. Honestly, it was finding volunteers. For example, in March only three students helped, but after I created a simple poster, the team grew from three to fifteen. If I may turn that question around, could you tell me what drew you to this episode? To sum up, if there is one key takeaway for the listeners, it is this: begin with people, not with posters. That experience taught me to ask for help early. Thanks again for having me.

feedback.es: Un buen invitado abre con cortesía, cuenta historias con ejemplos y cifras, devuelve una pregunta de sondeo y cierra con una síntesis.

origin.text: Eres invitado de un pódcast y te preguntan por un proyecto vecinal. Escribe 240–300 palabras: apertura cortés; una historia (situación, hecho anterior con pasado perfecto, acción y resultado con presente perfecto); un ejemplo con cifras; una pregunta de sondeo al anfitrión con «If I may turn that around…»; y un cierre con síntesis.

evidenceGroups: it is a pleasure to be

prompt.es: Escucha la reseña y elige qué da a entender el crítico sobre la invitada.

choices.text: That her honesty about failure earned more trust than polish would have.
That her polished delivery was what finally won him over.
That the host had prepared the interview less carefully than she had.
That she avoided the hardest question by asking a new one at once.

feedback.es: El crítico esperaba una presentación pulida y quedó conquistado («won over»): lo que más le impresionó fue que reconociera lo que salió mal, más que la perfección.

origin.audio: In his review of the podcast, the critic praised the guest for her preparation. She opened warmly, answered each question with a short story and never wasted a sentence. What impressed him most, however, came at the end. When the host pressed her on the weakest part of her project, she did not hide behind general phrases. She conceded a fair point, opened up about what had gone wrong and then turned the question around, asking the host how listeners usually respond to failure. The critic admitted that he had expected a polished sales pitch, and that he had been quietly won over instead.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere la productora en este correo sobre la entrevista grabada?

choices.text: That the host's question about the workshop pushed the guest back to her notes.
That the guest's best material came when she stopped following her notes.
That the guest's opening was strong, but her stories lacked figures and dates.
That the guest's closing takeaway was too vague to be edited well.

feedback.es: Señala que el mejor momento llegó cuando la invitada dejó de recitar y contó una historia con cifras: la espontaneidad superó al guion.

origin.text: I listened to the full recording again last night. For the first ten minutes, the guest seemed to be reading from her notes, and the answers felt flat. Then the host asked about the flooded workshop, and she told the story with real figures and dates. I would cut most of the opening and start the episode there.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tardé en abrirme y en contar lo que había pasado de verdad.»

feedback.es: Open up significa hablar con franqueza de algo personal; aquí, contar lo que ocurrió de verdad.

origin.text: I was nervous at first, and it took me a while to ___ up about what had really happened, but the listeners were kind.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe el anfitrión esta nota a su invitada?

choices.text: To ask her to replace the flooded garden story with a more recent one.
To warn her that listeners found the ending less memorable than the start.
To invite her to improve a good answer with one more figure.
To tell her that the next episode will focus on figures rather than stories.

feedback.es: La nota elogia la historia y pide solo una cifra más: su propósito es afinar una buena respuesta, no rechazarla ni cancelar nada.

origin.text: Thanks for agreeing to record again. Your story about the flooded garden was the heart of the last episode, and listeners loved it. Before we start, could you add one figure, such as how many volunteers came back afterwards? A number would make the ending even more memorable.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Déjame responder brevemente con una historia de mi primer año.»

answer.text: Let me answer briefly with a story from my first year

feedback.es: Let me answer briefly… anuncia una respuesta corta y estructurada con una historia.

prompt.es: Completa: «Dices que el club creció despacio; es una observación razonable.»

feedback.es: A fair point reconoce que el argumento del otro tiene parte de razón antes de matizarlo.

origin.text: You say that the club grew slowly, and that is a fair ___, although the figures since then tell a different story.
